d.chapter: Economic Geography — Sectors of the Economy
d.notions: Economy, economic activity, goods, services, raw material, production, sector of the economy.
d.focus: Introduction to the sectors of the economy; definitions of terms; key concepts (activities and examples).
d.competence: Learners are able to classify the jobs of people around them into the four sectors of the economy.
objectives: Define economy, economic activity, goods and services.
Define a sector of the economy.
Name the four sectors of the economy and give an example of each.
recall: In Lessons 1 to 4, we studied the natural regions of the world.
In each region, people carry out activities such as farming, rearing, mining and tourism.
These activities help them to earn a living.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: five jobs done in the family or neighbourhood.
situation: Ahmadou's father grows cotton near Garoua. His uncle works in the CICAM factory, where cotton becomes cloth. His aunt sells cloth in the Garoua market, and his cousin is a researcher who studies new cotton seeds.
Ahmadou's teacher says that all four people work in different sectors of the economy. Ahmadou does not understand what this means.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Ahmadou does not understand what the teacher means by the different sectors of the economy.
What does each member of Ahmadou's family do?
His father grows cotton, his uncle turns cotton into cloth, his aunt sells cloth, and his cousin studies new cotton seeds.
How can Ahmadou group these four jobs?
He can group them according to what they do: producing raw materials, transforming them, selling them, or creating knowledge.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand how the economy is organised and in which sector each job belongs.

qa.q: All the activities by which people produce, sell and buy things in a country form its ______. What is the missing word?
A tailor makes a dress, and a doctor treats a patient. Which one produces a good, and which one gives a service?
qa.a: The tailor produces a good, which is a thing we can touch. The doctor gives a service, which is work done for someone.

qa.q: Cotton is used to make cloth. What do we call a natural product used to make other goods?
qa.a: A natural product used to make other goods is called a raw material.

sum.title: I. Definitions
defs: The economy is the set of all the activities by which people produce, exchange and use goods and services.
An economic activity is any activity that people do to earn money or to satisfy their needs.
Goods are things that we can touch, such as food or clothes. Services are work done for others, such as teaching or transport.
A raw material is a natural product used to make other goods, such as cotton, wood or iron ore.
A sector of the economy is a group of economic activities of the same kind.

qa.q: Follow the journey of cotton.
Ahmadou's father takes cotton from nature. In which sector does he work?
qa.a: He works in the primary sector, which takes raw materials from nature.

qa.q: His uncle turns cotton into cloth, and his aunt sells the cloth. In which sectors do they work?
qa.a: His uncle works in the secondary sector, which transforms raw materials. His aunt works in the tertiary sector, which gives services.

qa.q: His cousin creates new knowledge about cotton. In which sector does she work?
qa.a: She works in the quaternary sector, which deals with research, knowledge and information.

sum.title: II. The Four Sectors of the Economy
sum.intro: The economy is divided into four sectors:
items: The primary sector takes raw materials from nature. Example: growing cotton.
The secondary sector transforms raw materials into finished goods. Example: making cloth from cotton.
The tertiary sector provides services to people. Example: selling cloth in the market.
The quaternary sector deals with research, knowledge and information. Example: creating better cotton seeds.

evaluation: What is the difference between a good and a service?
A good is a thing we can touch, like a shirt. A service is work done for others, like teaching.
In which sector does a fisherman work, and in which sector does a bank worker work?
A fisherman works in the primary sector, and a bank worker works in the tertiary sector.
Name the four sectors of the economy.
The four sectors are the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors.
remediation: A thing that we can touch, such as a shirt, is a ______.
Work done for others, such as teaching, is a ______.
A natural product used to make other goods is a ______ material.
The sector that takes raw materials from nature is the ______ sector.
The sector that transforms raw materials is the ______ sector.
The sector of research and information is the ______ sector.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. good 2. service 3. raw 4. primary 5. secondary 6. quaternary
d.homework: Observe two workers in your area: one who works for a registered company and one who works alone in the street (for example a moto-taxi driver). Write one difference between them.
d.homeworkTag: This prepares Part 2: The Formal and Informal Sectors of the Economy.
